newsitem.title: POLAND: France to boost investment in Polish agriculture.
newsitem.headline: France to boost investment in Polish agriculture.

text.p: France wants to increase its investment in Polish agriculture and boost food trade between the two countries before Poland joins the European Union at the turn of the century, the French agriculture minister said.

Philippe Vasseur told a news conference in Warsaw on Friday that France would also lend its political support for Poland to participate in the EU's common agricultre policy (CAP), but noted CAP would have to evolve to allow for new members.
"We would like to strengthen ties between Poland and France and increase French investment in Poland," Vasseur said.

"We will lend political support for Poland to participate in the EU's common agriculture policy as soon as possible...so that the agriuculture production of our countries is harmonised and competition between us fair," he said.

He said his visit was a follow-up to the recent Warsaw trip of French President Jacques Chirac, who made a welcome declaration that France would seek to catch up in investment in Poland with Germany -- the biggest EU investor in Poland.
Polish Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski, also present, said he invited French capital to enter Polish grain, potato, sugar, and edible fats sectors.
"I would be very happy to see French investment there," Jagielinski said.

Vasseur declined to give any details of the prospective investment, but several French businessmen accompanying him on the trip told reporters they were already in talks on cooperation or acquisitions in diary and edible fats sectors.
Vasseur also said France and Poland would seek to lower import tariffs and increase import quotas, but said all details would soon be discussed by groups of experts.
Poland had a $32 million deficit in food trade with France in the first half of this year against a $39 million gap in the whole of 1995.
